_note: Spoken-form variants of eval/cases.json's 40 cases, keyed by the same ids. Written 2026-11-16 for the v2 transcript bakeoff (handover docs/handovers/2026-11-16-claude-code-handover-nuance-live-persona.md §5.1) and WRITTEN BEFORE the runner was first executed - nothing here was edited after seeing a result, and eval/run-spoken-bakeoff.mjs says how to check that (git log on this file). They are HAND-WRITTEN, by a model, imagining how a person says the sentence aloud to an assistant. They are not transcripts of anybody. The real-ASR half of the experiment is eval/asr-roundtrip.py.

_kinds.disfluent: The same complaint with fillers, a repeat or a restart. Lowercase, no punctuation - the shape of an ASR transcript that does not punctuate.
_kinds.long: The same complaint behind the framing people put in front of one when they speak rather than type. Lowercase, no punctuation.
_kinds.vocative: The same complaint addressed to the assistant by name, as people address a face. Lowercase, no punctuation.
_kinds.asked: The same complaint put as a spoken QUESTION. This changes more than form - it changes grammatical mood - so the runner reports it SEPARATELY from the other three and it is not part of the headline delta.

vocativeProbes._note: Sentences that put the assistant's NAME through speech-to-text. The social layer strips the vocatives 'matic' and 'matic desk' (persona.json) so that a greeting addressed to the assistant is a greeting. If ASR writes the name another way, the residue rule sees a one-word complaint and the greeting goes to the model. Each entry is the sentence as typed and the classification it gets as typed.
probes: hello matic how are you today
